guide_enrichment.narrative:
For us, the case for BYU starts with an offense that has more than one way to sustain drives. BYU averaged 262.7 rushing yards through three games and topped 300 yards twice, while allowing only two sacks over that span. We are not treating that early production as proof against a much stronger opponent, but the combination of rushing efficiency and protection gives BYU a plausible path to avoid the kind of negative plays that create separation.

The meaningful concern is Notre Dame's defense. Our metrics rate its pass defense first in pass EPA and place it among the best units at preventing scoring opportunities. That matters because our longer-run numbers are less impressed with BYU's passing offense than its early results might suggest, even though Bear Bachmeier opened the season with 642 passing yards, six touchdowns and one interception through three games.

Notre Dame's fourth-ranked passing offense also presents a real challenge for BYU's pass defense. Still, BYU intercepted five passes in its first three games, and we see enough resistance on both sides of the ball to question whether Notre Dame should be priced to create this much separation. Our wager is less about declaring BYU the better team and more about taking the points at a number our model considers too high.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch:
We are watching BYU's passing game against Notre Dame's pass defense. Notre Dame owns the clearest matchup advantage in our numbers, so BYU cannot depend on routine dropback success. The more interesting part is whether BYU's rushing attack can keep Bachmeier out of predictable passing situations and preserve manageable downs.

If BYU can do that, its early pass protection gives the offense a chance to stay functional even without consistently winning through the air. If Notre Dame forces obvious passing downs, its defensive advantage becomes much more likely to control the game.

recent_game.fact: BYU defeated Colorado State 41-23 in Fort Collins to improve to 3-0.
BYU rushed for 332 yards against Colorado State, including 176 yards and three touchdowns from LJ Martin and 131 yards and one rushing touchdown from wide receiver Legend Glasker.
BYU held Colorado State to 302 total yards after Colorado State entered averaging 469.0 yards per game.

quarterback.fact: Sophomore Bear Bachmeier had started all 17 of his career games, including BYU's first three games of 2026.
Through three games, Bachmeier had completed 44 of 62 passes for 642 yards, six touchdowns and one interception while rushing for 64 yards and two touchdowns.
Bachmeier led the Big 12 with a 186.7 passing-efficiency rating and 10.35 yards per pass attempt through three games.
Treyson Bourguet, a Western Michigan transfer with eight previous career starts, was listed as Bachmeier's primary backup.

offensive_personnel.fact: Running back LJ Martin had 328 rushing yards and three touchdowns on 42 carries through three games, averaging 7.8 yards per carry.
Freshman wide receiver Legend Glasker had 270 receiving yards and two receiving touchdowns on 11 catches, plus 42 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns, through three games.
USC transfer Walker Lyons started each of BYU's first three games at tight end and caught multiple passes in every game.
Oregon transfer Roger Saleapaga II started BYU's first two games at tight end, while Keayen Nead started at Colorado State.

BYU's offensive line starters against Colorado State were Paki Finau at left tackle, Sonny Makasini at left guard, Bruce Mitchell at center, Trevin Ostler at right guard and Andrew Gentry at right tackle.
Paki Finau, a Washington transfer, started the first three games at left tackle; Andrew Gentry, a Michigan transfer, started the first three games at right tackle.
Center Bruce Mitchell moved from defensive line to offensive line in 2024 and entered 2026 after earning first-team All-Big 12 honors in 2025.

defensive_personnel.fact: Cal transfer Cade Uluave started the first three games at linebacker and recorded 14 tackles, two tackles for loss and one interception.
Defensive tackle Keanu Tanuvasa started all three games and recorded four tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss and a half-sack.
Cannon DeVries started two of the first three games at nickel and had a team-high 14 tackles through three games, including three tackles for loss at Colorado State.
Cornerbacks Therrian Alexander III and Evan Johnson and safety Faletau Satuala started each of BYU's first three games.
BYU had five interceptions through three games, with one each by Therrian Alexander III, Hunter Clegg, Evan Johnson, Matthias Leach and Cade Uluave.

injury_availability.fact: Linebacker Siale Esera was explicitly listed as out for BYU's game at Colorado State.
Safety Raider Damuni was injured against Utah Tech and had appeared in only one of BYU's first three games.
